topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the scope of the lecture series, the interdisciplinary student audience, and the key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Biological foundations of cancer and experimental models
topics.groupedBecause: They define cancer as a multistep disruption of genetic integrity and tissue differentiation programs, highlighting the methods and limitations of studying these processes in culture.

topics.label: Tumour invasion, metastasis, and stepwise progression
topics.groupedBecause: They describe how tumors progress from contained, benign precursor lesions to invasive and metastatic malignancies, contrasting their macroscopic and histological behaviors.

topics.label: Conventions and exceptions of tumour nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic establishes the standard medical naming rules and key exceptions used to classify benign and malignant tumors based on their tissue of origin.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the local, systemic, and metastatic processes by which tumor growth causes organ failure, illness, and patient death.

topics.label: Tumour incidence across human tissues and animal species
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the statistical prevalence of various tumor types in humans and compare incidence across animal species to frame cancer as a universal consequence of multicellularity.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the clinical presentation of tumors and the utility, techniques, and limitations of population screening programmes for identifying pre-malignant lesions.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by revisiting the learning outcomes and providing housekeeping notes for upcoming practicals and lectures.
